prompt: A photorealistic top-down photograph of a spiral notice display, blue pins set along a spiral guide line. The objects follow a single spiral that winds outward from the centre for EXACTLY 3 full turns, with EXACTLY 7 objects evenly spaced on each turn, so there are 3 turns x 7 per turn = EXACTLY 21 objects in total -- not 20, not 22. Each object is separate and clearly visible along the spiral. No text, no numerals.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show small objects arranged in a single spiral winding outward from the centre, with the same number of objects on each turn of the spiral? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q: How many blue pins are in this image? They are arranged along a spiral; count every one along the whole spiral from centre to edge. Count them one by one. Answer with the integer number only.
reference.q_notext: Does this image have any printed number, digit, numeral, written label or caption overlaid on it (as opposed to being purely a photograph / drawing of the scene with no text)? Answer yes if you can see ANY printed number or word, no if there is none. Answer yes or no only.
reference.d2_q_objform: This picture should show these countable objects: small objects arranged in a single spiral winding outward from the centre, with the same number of objects on each turn of the spiral. Look at the individual objects being counted. Is each one an object set along the spiral, and not some other object, a shapeless blob, or a mixture of different things? Answer with the single word yes or no only.
reference.d2_q_occlusion: Look at the objects being counted in this image. Is EVERY one of them visible as its own separate individual (allowing for the intended overlaps/stacking the scene describes), rather than merged into one indistinct blob? Answer yes if each intended object can be told apart, no if they merge into an uncountable mass. Answer with the single word yes or no only.

steps.read_crop: Does this picture show one {gt.target_color} object -- for example a {gt.target_color} plant, a {gt.target_color} disc, a {gt.target_color} stud head or a {gt.target_color} pin head set on the surface? Answer no if the thing you can see is a clearly different colour, or if there is no such object here at all, only bare ground, gravel, stone, board or background. Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Does this image show small objects arranged along a single spiral that winds outward from the centre? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: one blue pin set along the spiral guide line of the notice display, seen from straight above

steps.read_crop: Does this cut-out show ONE whole blue pin sitting on the spiral guide line, rather than a pin of some other colour, some other object, bare board, a shapeless blob, or only part of a pin? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: a clump on the spiral where several blue pins merge together so they cannot be told apart
